title: Shadowfang Keep
body: Shadowfang Keep crowns the heights above Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine. It was the seat of Baron Silverlaine until the worgen loosed on the forest turned on the living and laid siege to it, and the keep fell into shadow and ruin. Now it belongs to Arugal, the archmage whose magic brought them. He keeps to the top of the keep's tower, the worgen he calls his sons prowl its halls and walls, and Fenrus, a wolf of enormous size, guards the way up to him. The keep's dead have not left. The ghosts of its servants, guardsmen and officers still walk its rooms, and the baron himself is said to haunt the place. Just inside the gate a worgen cell keeper holds prisoners, and a heavy door shuts off the courtyard beyond. Few come here by choice. The Forsaken want word of their missing deathstalkers, and a keeper in the Undercity wants a book of Dalaran lore said to be somewhere within.

parts.body: Odo the Blindwatcher, a worgen sentry, keeps watch on the walk that leads from the keep's halls toward the tower. The moment intruders reach him he calls the beasts nearby to his side, and the more he is wounded the more his howling rage swells. It did not save him, and the Blindwatcher fell at his post.

title: The Cells
body: Just inside the keep's gate, a row of barred cells serves Arugal as a prison. Rethilgore, a worgen called the Cell Keeper, stands guard over them with whitescalp worgen about him, and levers set in the walls work the cell doors. Three prisoners wait behind the bars: a human sorcerer named Ashcrombe, a Forsaken deathstalker named Adamant, and a man called Landen Stilwell. Past the cells, the door into the keep's courtyard stays firmly shut.

parts.body: Rethilgore fought for his cells to the last, holding his foes fast while he drained the life out of them. When the Cell Keeper fell, his prisoners spoke up at once. The deathstalker remarked that it was about time someone killed the wretch, and a moment later the sorcerer agreed with him, for once, though he still called him scum.

parts.body: Ashcrombe is glad to talk. The Kirin Tor sent him from Dalaran to learn how Arugal's work against the undead of Silverpine was faring, never guessing that the wizard had lost his grip on sanity. He must report the whole sorry business at once, but first he offers to undo the magical lock on the courtyard door for whoever cut down Rethilgore, who may yet survive what lies beyond.

parts.body: Adamant has a report to make. High Executor Hadrec sent him and Vincent, another deathstalker, to spy out the keep so that a plan could be laid to overthrow Arugal for good. But the old wizard has many tricks, and a magical ward gave them away. Adamant was thrown into this cell. Vincent, he says, was not so lucky. Adamant must hurry back to Hadrec, but first he will pick the lock on the courtyard door.

title: The Courtyard
body: Past the cells, the courtyard door opens on the open heart of the keep. Shadowfang moonwalkers prowl the yard, the restless spirits of the keep's servants drift through it, and in the stables at its far end fel steeds stand in the stalls. Off the yard lies the kitchen, where the fires still roar and a worgen butcher holds sway, and beyond it the way runs on into the keep's great hall and the floors above.

parts.body: Razorclaw the Butcher kept the kitchen among its roaring fires, a worgen at home at the chopping block. He fought savagely and drained the magic from those who stood against him, but the butcher fell at last on his own kitchen floor.

title: Baron Silverlaine
body: Baron Silverlaine was lord of this keep when the worgen came to Silverpine. They besieged his home until it fell into shadow and ruin, and the baron did not live through it. His spirit has not left. A pale ghost, he keeps to the great hall beyond the kitchen, where the shades of the keep's servants still drift and worgen gluttons sit among crates of food and barrels of melon juice. It is said that his vengeful ghost haunts Arugal himself.

parts.body: The baron met intruders with a veil of shadow that withered every healing touch his foes received, and he gave no ground. It was not enough. The ghost of Baron Silverlaine was struck down in his own hall, and the shades around him went on drifting as before.

title: Commander Springvale
body: Commander Springvale is one more of the keep's dead who will not rest. His ghost holds the keep's upper floor among the wailing spirits of guardsmen, while the shades of tormented officers keep watch along the walls, as though the garrison still stood to its duty. He bears a commander's rank still, and he fights as a paladin of the Light once did, calling on a holy power that death has not taken from him.

parts.body: Springvale still had the Light at his call. As his foes wore him down he closed his own wounds with holy light, and when he was hard pressed he wrapped himself in its protection. None of it saved him. The commander fell at last, and his guardsmen went on wailing in the halls.

title: Fenrus the Devourer
body: Fenrus the Devourer is Arugal's pet, a wolf of enormous size, and it is said that the archmage counts on him for protection. He lairs in a chamber partway up the keep's tower, on the only way to his master's rooms, with the Sons of Arugal and lupine horrors prowling the tower around him. Above his chamber, on a high ledge, stands a focus of Arugal's magic, and past it a sealed gate bars the way on.

parts.body: Fenrus fought with a venomous slaver that burned his foes and sapped their magic. When the great wolf died, Arugal's voice rang through the tower, demanding to know who dared interfere with the Sons of Arugal. Moments later his focus above the chamber stirred, and voidwalkers appeared and fell upon the intruders, mending one another with dark offerings as they fought.

title: Wolf Master Nandos
body: Wolf Master Nandos is the worgen who keeps the beasts of Shadowfang, and he stands near the top of the tower before the door of Arugal's Lair. He does not stand alone. His pack waits at his side, a lupine horror and worgs of every breed the keep holds, and while he lives the door to his master's chamber stays shut.

parts.body: When the last beast of his pack fell, Nandos could not believe it. They had destroyed his pack, he howled, and now they would face his wrath. He called fresh beasts to his side as he fought, but the wolf master fell all the same, and with his death the door of Arugal's Lair swung open.

title: The Master of Shadowfang
body: Shadowfang Keep is Arugal's now. The archmage of the Kirin Tor whose summoned worgen overran Silverpine has made the baron's home his own, and he calls the worgen his children. The Sons of Arugal stalk the tower beneath his rooms, carrying his dark gift that withers those they strike, and the Shadowfang worgen hold the halls and walls below. He keeps to the topmost chamber of the tower, behind Fenrus and his wolf master, and from there his voice can carry through the keep. Those who would reach him face a long climb through his creatures, and at the end of it a madman.

parts.body: Arugal met intruders in his chamber with a promise that they too would serve. He hurled bolts of void, stunned those around him with a thundering shock, and vanished in shadow only to reappear elsewhere in the room. Worst was his curse. Crying out to release their rage, he turned one of his attackers into a worgen glutton and set the beast against its friends. Whenever one fell, he gloated that another had fallen. But in the end the archmage fell himself.

title: Deathstalkers in Shadowfang
body: At the Sepulcher in Silverpine, High Executor Hadrec is still waiting for a report that has not come. Ahead of an assault on Shadowfang Keep, two deathstalkers, Adamant and Vincent, were sent into the keep to gather intelligence. Many days have passed and neither has returned, yet without their findings the Forsaken have little hope of a successful attack. Hadrec wants both of them found, and helped if they need it. The mission, he warns, is as dangerous as it is critical, and failure is not to be thought of.

parts.body: Vincent was found at last, his body broken and still. Adamant would carry his own report back to Hadrec, but whatever more Vincent had learned in the keep would stay with him. All he still held was a small trinket, clutched in his hand, and it went back with the one who found him.
sources: quest 1098 reward text (Vincent's body lies broken, and still; Adamant will send his report to Hadrec; whatever additional details Vincent gained must remain with him; clutched in his hand is a small trinket)

title: The Book of Ur
body: In the Apothecarium of the Undercity, Keeper Bel'dugur has his eye on a book. It lies somewhere in Shadowfang Keep: the Book of Ur, written by a great mage of Dalaran in the days before the Scourge came. Ur studied other worlds, and that work, the keeper says, is of real value to certain parties among the Forsaken, though he does not say who they are. The book would be a prize for his collection, and whoever brings it to him will have the service reported to the Dark Lady herself.

parts.body: The book came back from the keep. Ur wrote it to catalogue the fiends of other worlds, and its pages describe the worgen: real beasts from a dark place of nightmare, drawn into this world only by powerful magic. He hoped no wizard of Dalaran would ever seek them out. Bel'dugur was pleased. Ur's knowledge was great, he said, but his conscience held him back from true power, and when the Scourge tested him it failed. The Forsaken cannot afford such weakness.

title: Jordan's Hammer
body: In Ironforge, the smith Jordan Stilwell owes a paladin more than he can repay, and means to forge a holy weapon in thanks. His notes list what he needs, and one item lies in Shadowfang Keep. Before the plague, Jordan lived in Pyrewood, and it was in the keep above the village that he learned the secret of steel. When he and his wife escaped from it they left precious things behind, among them the smithing hammer his father gave him. His father always swore it was enchanted, and it is the last reminder Jordan has of him, for the Scourge killed him. It lies in the stables of the keep's courtyard, unless the creatures there have taken up smithing.

parts.body: Jordan had everything he needed at last. He had kept the plans for this weapon for a long time, he admitted, and only lacked the chance to gather the goods. Holding his father's hammer again felt good, and he set to the forge.
sources: quest 1654 reward text (I've actually had the plans for doing this for some time; I just never had the opportunity to gather the goods; it feels good to have my father's hammer again)

parts.body: The weapon was finished at Jordan's forge. He named it for a great dwarven paladin who had been his friend, Bosch Verigan, and gave it on behalf of himself and his wife, for the world, he said, would be a safer place with such a champion of the Light abroad.

title: The Bloodforged Ingots
body: Knight-Lord Bloodvalor's notes for a new adept of the Blood Knights list the makings of the order's blood-tempered ranseur, and one of them is hidden in Shadowfang Keep. Bloodforged ingots are a superior metal made by a well-kept secret, and rumor says any smith who works them is cursed, though the order's craftsmen claim to have proved the tale false. The Forsaken have sent word that a supply may be found in the keep. A skilled smith named Landen Stilwell grew curious enough to smuggle a crate of the ingots inside. No one knows where he hid it, but the smith himself is said to be a prisoner in the keep's dungeon, and any means may be used to get the ingots.

parts.body: The crate was found in the stables off the keep's courtyard, where Stilwell had hidden it, and it was carried back to Silvermoon with everything else the notes demanded. Bloodvalor looked it over and was satisfied. All that remained, he said, was to forge the weapon.
